correctness.rationale: On the stated stationary branch, the exact liquid and gas flux profiles give a normalized first radial moment after two justified integrals. The relation mu=q^2/(q-1) simplifies its expression and the exact derivative is (2-q)/q^3 times [(c-1)-q(q+2)/6]. The second factor is strictly decreasing in q, and mu decreases strictly with q. This proves all global monotonicity, uniqueness, and endpoint assertions. Independent numerical spatial quadrature verified 199 cases; proof does not rely on tests. Critical profiles and parameter normalization are in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: The assessed result is the entire mean-radius response when gas-crowding mu varies at fixed reset rate and fixed total mass, including two exact dimensionless thresholds. Grange gives the stationary profiles and an optimization of droplet width against reset rate, not this contrary localization response. Closest available work compares gas-vs-droplet radial transport at fixed crowding and optimizes W_infinity in reset rate; another extends dense-core flux and width optimization. Although the mean formula is directly calculable from published profiles and can be related to the earlier W1 integral, the distinct global crowding-axis trichotomy is not asserted or derived in examined sources. A residual risk is unindexed equivalent analysis.
residual_risks: Published stationary profiles and a closely related gas-versus-droplet transport integral make the mean formula a relatively short mathematical derivation; novelty rests on the parameter-dependent global classification and its physical contrast.
Relevant unindexed, unpublished, or differently named calculations might contain the same thresholds; absence from searches is not proof of publication priority.
Dynamical stability, microscopic validation and finite-size response are not established.

value.rationale: A spatially averaged radial distance is a motivated localization observable complementary to density profile and half-width. The theorem reveals increasing global spread while the concentrated core width decreases, characterizes a genuine finite interior maximum, and provides exact universal dimensionless c boundaries for all fixed positive rates and masses with c>1.
